answer: Admission is a cross-branch quorum: a new voice needs a quill from two separate branches and locks 1 plume in each; the hollow records which branches signed and merges voices whose quorums touch. A same operator’s kth voice must clear k+1 fresh branches, 1 plume each, while earlier plume stays locked; overlap collapses it to a single ballot. Honest start: 2 plume. n clones pay 2+…+(n+1) plume to unrelated branches.
